The primitives describe a hierarchical cognitive process where rats form sign gestalt expectations from sensory inputs, compress these into condensed features, and maintain them across delays to guide future behavior. This process involves three core operations: (1) gestalt condensation—whereby a full sign is reduced to a salient feature; (2) delayed retention—preserving the gestalt expectation over time; and (3) retrieval-driven execution—using the condensed feature to re-trigger the full gestalt. These operations are mathematically modeled as a sequence of transformations: S → F → G → B, where S is sensory input, F is feature, G is gestalt expectation, and B is behavior. Each step introduces a form of abstraction or compression, enabling temporal anticipation. The system exhibits duality between perception and action, where prior knowledge is encoded in symbolic form and retrieved under delayed conditions. Failure modes arise when abstraction is insufficient or retention is unstable. The model supports retroactive inference of learning dynamics through Bayesian belief updates.
